business_question: What evidence can you find whether or not the "women and children first" principle applied during that time period on the Titanic?
business_answer_shown: The survival outcomes are consistent with the "women and children first" principle: adult women had a 76.8% survival rate and children under age 16 had a 57.4% survival rate, compared with only 17.7% for adult men. These differences provide strong descriptive evidence of preferential survival for women and children, although survival rates alone do not prove the specific evacuation procedures or their causal effect.

baseline_chart_assessment.why_it_matters: Business managers should be able to understand the central finding immediately rather than infer the answer from three bars.
baseline_chart_assessment.related_principle: Story / Method - Tell the Story with the Title

baseline_chart_assessment.issue: All three groups use the same visual emphasis even though the key comparison is women and children versus adult men.
baseline_chart_assessment.why_it_matters: Equal visual treatment makes the viewer perform more work to identify the comparison that answers the business question.

baseline_chart_assessment.issue: The baseline communicates the survival-rate differences but does not distinguish descriptive evidence from proof that a particular evacuation procedure caused those outcomes.
baseline_chart_assessment.why_it_matters: The business question asks whether the principle appears to have applied; the visualization should communicate the evidence without overstating causal certainty.

data_fidelity_checks.check: Adult women survival rate and denominator
data_fidelity_checks.notes: Source data verification produced 255 survivors among 332 adult women with known age, or 76.8%, matching the baseline.
Using the supplied definition of children as passengers under age 16, source data verification produced 66 survivors among 115 children with known age, or 57.4%, matching the baseline.

data_fidelity_checks.check: Adult men survival rate and denominator
data_fidelity_checks.notes: Source data verification produced 106 survivors among 599 adult men with known age, or 17.7%, matching the baseline.
There are 263 records without usable age values. They were excluded consistently because classification into child versus adult cannot be supported from the supplied age field.
The improved chart retains survival rate as a percentage on a 0-100% scale and preserves all substantive relationships shown by the baseline.

baseline_to_improved_comparison.baseline: Shows 76.8% for adult women, 57.4% for children, and 17.7% for adult men.
baseline_to_improved_comparison.improved: Preserves the same verified rates and denominators: adult women 76.8% (n=332), children 57.4% (n=115), and adult men 17.7% (n=599).

remaining_limitations: The chart is descriptive and cannot by itself establish that an explicit evacuation policy caused the observed survival differences.
Passengers with missing age are excluded because they cannot be reliably classified as children or adults from the supplied data.
The aggregate comparison does not control for passenger class, location aboard the ship, lifeboat access, family relationships, or other factors that may also be associated with survival.
